## Objective

Implement a distinct reusable What Did You Learn module that turns relevant evidence into supported lessons, concrete improvement dispositions and useful later behavior, and include it in new and existing Sys4AI initialization.

User value: Agents can learn from material discussions and work while retaining evidence, ownership, privacy, project settings and predictable adoption.

### Success outcomes

- One discoverable manual review and coordinated completion workflow uses the existing memory system.
- New, first-prepared and explicitly selected prior-edition projects receive compatible local module capability with preserved content and accurate provenance.
- A bounded authorized learning scenario demonstrates publication, canonical retrieval, improvement disposition and comparable later use.
- All 28 source requirements and their acceptance criteria have traceable implementation and verification work.

## Scope

### In scope

- LEARNING-depo policy/contracts/assets and the thin what-did-you-learn skill.
- Shared memory checkpoint, supported evidence/lifecycle, ordinary read preservation, opt-out, current manager ownership and frozen inputs.
- Default v7 create/first preparation and explicitly selected prior-edition module adoption with compatible dependency handling and existing receipt recovery.
- Updater-managed Template distribution, exact active-root package adoption and relevant documentation.
- Automated checks and isolated native learning, initialization, publication, retrieval and comparable-use scenarios; complete final audit.

### Out of scope

- A second memory store, Task/setup ledger, permanent learning manager or mandatory agent team.
- Runtime hooks WDYL-H1/WDYL-H2, inactivity scheduling, background consolidation, transcript recording and model-weight training.
- Automatic propagation to unspecified projects, copying learned history or source grants, and silent custom-package overwrites.
- Unnecessary memory schema/trigger extensions, dependency/backend provisioning, retired-system restoration, external tickets, Git publication and deployment.
- Changes to the current to-trd implementation without a demonstrated authorized defect; its handoff example is hypothetical.
- Execution, project initialization, publication of learned records, or Task/TRD mutation during this planning operation.

### Execution authority

This plan records proposed work. Creating or approving it does not authorize implementation, installation, memory publication, project adoption, Task/TRD activation, Git publication, deployment or any other separately governed action. Execution requires separate authorization of the exact plan through the applicable project workflow, including its declared isolated verification scenarios.

### Constraints

- Plan creation changes only the selected managed plan and its generated catalog index.
- Author reusable changes in source collections; the updater owns Template destinations; root adoption uses an exact reviewed manifest.
- Keep Python 3.12 standard-library helper operation; no dependency, backend, runtime hook, model, service or external installation.
- Use existing canonical memory, publication, Task and setup contracts; only the bounded initializer edition/module receipt extension is proposed.
- Preserve already-bound governance, memory settings, opt-out, learned history, old receipt semantics, role casing, licensing and unrelated Git edits.
- Implementation evidence must distinguish static checks, helper fixtures, native behavior, canonical publication, retrieval and comparable later use.
- Native Task scenarios need the existing workflow authority, true owner, initial write scope, fresh roles and inherited model/effort; no extra permanent team is introduced.
